holidays.name: National Cereal Day
holidays.description: A crunchy, milky celebration of the breakfast bowl. Fans pour a heaping serving of their favorite flakes, puffs, or marshmallow-studded morsels, and some eat it for dinner as well.
holidays.origin: Its exact origin is unclear. It is an unofficial food holiday that spread through food-industry calendars and social media, and it sits near the March 7 anniversary of the cereal-loving 19th-century health reform movement in Battle Creek, Michigan.
holidays.funFact: Cereal was invented as a health food. Corn flakes were created in the 1890s by the Kellogg brothers as a bland breakfast meant to promote wholesome living.

holidays.name: National Crown Roast of Pork Day
holidays.description: A celebration of the fancy roast made from rib sections of pork tied into a circle, so it looks like a royal crown. It is the dish that says you have your life together, or at least a very large oven.
holidays.origin: Crown roast of pork is a classic centerpiece for holiday feasts. The food day is an unofficial observance that arose from food-themed calendars.
holidays.funFact: The bones of a crown roast are traditionally topped with little paper frills called chops frills, which are sometimes jokingly referred to as chef hats for the bones.

holidays.name: National Be Heard Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to speaking up, sharing your ideas, and making sure your voice is heard, whether you are telling the boss about your great idea or telling the dog to get off the couch.
holidays.origin: It is an unofficial awareness observance promoted by communication and self-expression advocates, aimed at encouraging people to share their opinions and ideas.
holidays.funFact: Alexander Graham Bell was awarded the patent for the telephone on March 7, 1876, so this date really is a good one for being heard.

holidays.name: Alexander Graham Bell Telephone Patent Anniversary
holidays.description: The anniversary of the day the telephone patent was officially issued, which changed forever how people yell, 'Can you hear me now?'
holidays.origin: US Patent No. 174,465 was granted to Alexander Graham Bell on March 7, 1876, covering a method of transmitting speech telegraphically. Three days later he made the first successful call to his assistant.
holidays.funFact: The first words spoken over the telephone were reportedly 'Mr. Watson, come here, I want to see you,' and Bell had spilled battery acid on himself at the time.

holidays.name: Panic Day
holidays.description: A tongue-in-cheek holiday where you are invited to run around in a mild frenzy, flap your arms, and worry about things you possibly do not need to worry about, ideally in good fun.
holidays.origin: Panic Day is a humorous unofficial observance that appears in quirky holiday calendars, created as a stress-release joke for people who spend the rest of the year trying to stay calm.
holidays.funFact: The word panic comes from the Greek god Pan, whose sudden shouts in the wilderness were said to send travelers and livestock into irrational terror.
